# Getting Started

# Getting Started

aris-ui is a modern C++20 immediate-mode UI library for OpenGL. It renders
widgets as analytically anti-aliased signed-distance fields, draws text from
offline-generated MSDF atlases, lays out panels with Yoga flexbox, and leaves
the host's OpenGL state exactly as it found it.

## Requirements

- CMake 3.20+
- A C++20 compiler (GCC 11+, Clang 13+, MSVC 2019+)
- OpenGL 3.3 (GL 2.1 / 150-core variants are planned — Stage 10)
- FreeType (development package) for the atlas generator

## Build

```sh
git clone <repo> aris-ui && cd aris-ui
make configure     # = cmake -S . -B build -DARIS_UI_BUILD_TESTS=ON
make build         # = cmake --build build
make test          # unit tests (ctest)
make preview       # headless UI snapshots → previews/*.png
make demo          # interactive desktop runner window
```

No package hunting: Yoga, msdfgen, glad, stb and nlohmann/json are vendored
and pinned under `third_party/`. Only GLFW (for the examples) is fetched by
CMake at configure time.

## Your first frame

aris-ui is caller-driven: *you* own the frame loop and the GL context, the
library never touches a window, swaps a buffer, or starts a thread.

```cpp
#include "ui/aris_ui.hpp"
#include "atlas_generator/atlas_gen.hpp"

ui::Context ctx;                 // one per process
ui::FontAtlas font;
font.Load("atlas/ui.png", "atlas/ui.json");
ctx.SetTheme(ui::Theme::Default());
ctx.SetFont(&font);

// --- your render loop, every frame ---
ui::GlStateGuard guard;          // snapshots ALL relevant GL state
ctx.BeginFrame(dt, width, height);
ctx.ProcessInput(event);         // translated host events (see Core Concepts)

ctx.BeginPanel("main", ui::Rect(28, 28, 470, 640),
               ui::PanelStyle::FromTheme(ui::Theme::Default(), 18.f, "Hello"));
if (ui::Button(ctx, "Click me")) ++clicks;
ui::Toggle(ctx, "Enabled", &enabled);
ui::Slider(ctx, "Opacity", &opacity, 0.f, 1.f);
ctx.EndPanel();

ctx.Render();                    // layout + draw; guard restores host state
```

Generating the font atlas (offline, cached — regenerate only when the font
changes):

```cpp
std::string err;
ui_atlas::Params params;                 // fontSize 48, pxRange 4, ASCII + extras
ui_atlas::GenerateAndWrite("font.ttf", "atlas/ui", params, err);
```

Or from the command line: `./build/atlasgen <font.ttf> <out-prefix>`.

## Integration checklist

1. Translate your platform input into `ui::InputEvent` variants and feed each
   one to `ctx.ProcessInput()` before drawing.
2. Wrap `ctx.Render()` in a `ui::GlStateGuard` so your own pipeline state
   (blend, depth, VAOs, program) survives the UI pass untouched.
3. Draw the UI **last**, after your scene, with depth testing disabled.

## Next steps

- [Core Concepts](core-concepts.html) — the frame lifecycle and state model
- [Widgets](widgets.html) — the built-in control set and theming tokens
- [Layout](layout.html) — panels, rows, columns and flexbox styling
- [Rendering](rendering.html) — SDF shader contract and the batcher
- [Fonts](fonts.html) — the MSDF atlas pipeline and JSON schema
- [Agent Tooling](agent-tooling.html) — previews, tests and docs for coding agents

# Core Concepts

# Core Concepts

aris-ui follows an immediate-mode *API over retained state* model: your code
declares the UI every frame like Dear ImGui, while the library retains the
expensive parts (widget state, Yoga layout tree, GPU batches) between frames.

## The frame lifecycle

```cpp
ctx.BeginFrame(dt, width, height);   // clock, mouse, hot-widget recomputation
ctx.ProcessInput(event);             // feed translated host events (optional, per event)
// ... declare your UI with BeginPanel / widgets / DrawText / DrawRect ...
ctx.Render();                        // run layout, flush draw commands to GL
```

- `BeginFrame` rolls the rect registry: rects computed last frame drive input
  and drawing this frame (**one-frame latency** — an egui-style tradeoff that
  keeps layout and hit-testing decoupled).
- `ProcessInput` returns `true` when the UI consumed an event (e.g. a click on
  a widget). Consume policy: the UI blocks events that hit interactive
  widgets, everything else passes through to the host.
- `Render` runs the Yoga layout pass, resolves widget rects, and replays the
  recorded command queue through the batcher.

## Events

The host translates platform input into a `std::variant`:

```cpp
using InputEvent = std::variant<
    MouseMoveEvent,      // Vec2 pos
    MouseButtonEvent,    // button, pressed, pos
    MouseScrollEvent,    // delta, pos
    KeyEvent,            // key code, pressed, repeat
    TextInputEvent>;     // codepoint
```

Mouse coordinates are in the same pixel space the UI is drawn in (y-down,
origin top-left). There is no inversion, no scaling — translate 1:1.

## Retained state

`WidgetStateStore` keeps one `WidgetState` per widget ID (FNV-1a hash of the
label + the ID stack):

```cpp
struct WidgetState {
    float hoverT;      // eased 0..1 hover amount
    float pressT;      // eased 0..1 press amount
    float valueT;      // widget value (e.g. toggle knob position)
};
```

Targets are set by widgets each frame; `Advance()` eases them with a
frame-rate-independent exponential filter (`ExpSmooth`, ~14/s for hover,
~22/s for press). Un-touched states are garbage-collected after 240 frames.

## Widget IDs

IDs are derived from the string label combined with the container ID stack, so
identical labels in different panels never collide. Hashing is deterministic
(FNV-1a 64, tested against published reference vectors).

## Drawing primitives

You rarely need these, but they are the public surface everything else uses:

```cpp
ctx.DrawRect(const Rect& rect, const RectStyle& style);
ctx.DrawText(Vec2 pos, std::string_view utf8, const Color& color,
             float fontSize, const Rect* clipRect = nullptr);
Vec2 ctx.MeasureText(std::string_view utf8, float fontSize) const;
```

`RectStyle` packs fill, per-corner radii, border and a soft drop shadow
(offset / spread / blur / opacity). `DrawText` decodes UTF-8, walks glyph
quads, and clips against `clipRect` (passing your panel content rect is the
convention).

## Command queue

`ctx.Render()` first records a frame's worth of POD commands
(`RoundedRect`, `Glyph`, `ClipPush`/`ClipPop`) into a `ui::CommandQueue`,
then replays them through the OpenGL batcher. The queue is pure data — you can
inspect it headlessly (the test suite does exactly that) or replay it with
your own backend later.

## What the library does NOT do

- No windowing, no threading, no buffer swapping — the host owns the loop.
- No global state, no singletons: one `ui::Context` per process, pass it around.
- No rendering beyond GL 3.3 core today (older variants are roadmap Stage 10).

---

# Widgets

# Widgets

All widgets are free functions taking the context first. They require an
active panel (`BeginPanel`/`EndPanel`) because layout belongs to the Yoga
tree. Every widget draws *and* handles input in the same call.

```cpp
#include "ui/widgets/widgets.hpp"
```

## API

| Function | Signature | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Button | `bool Button(Context&, const char* label)` | Returns true on the frame the click completes (press + release inside). |
| Toggle | `void Toggle(Context&, const char* label, bool* value)` | Flips `*value` when clicked; knob position eases via `valueT`. |
| Slider | `void Slider(Context&, const char* label, float* value, float minValue, float maxValue)` | Updates `*value` while dragged; shows a right-aligned value label. |
| Label | `void Label(Context&, const char* text, Color color = {}, float fontSize = 0.f)` | Static text; `fontSize = 0` uses the theme default. |

## Visual states

Colors and shadows ease through `WidgetStateStore` — buttons lift on hover
(`hoverT`) and settle when pressed (`pressT`), toggles slide their knob with
`valueT`. The states are frame-rate independent (exponential smoothing), so
animations look identical at 60 or 240 fps.

| State | Fill | Shadow |
| --- | --- | --- |
| idle | `accent` | opacity 0.18, offset (0,2) |
| hover | `accentHover` | opacity 0.32, offset (0,5) |
| press | `accentActive` | opacity 0.08, offset (0,2) |

You can inspect a widget's eased state yourself via
`ctx.theme()` + `WidgetStateStore` if you build custom controls.

## Custom widgets

Custom controls are just immediate-mode code using the primitives:

```cpp
void ColorDot(ui::Context& ctx, ui::Color color) {
    ui::WidgetFrame w = ctx.BeginWidget("dot", 20.f);
    if (w.rect.Valid()) {
        ui::RectStyle st;
        st.fill = color;
        st.cornerRadii = ui::Vec4(10.f);
        ctx.DrawRect(w.rect, st);
    }
    ctx.EndWidget();
}
```

`BeginWidget(label, height)` creates a full-width flexbox row of the given
height inside the current panel and returns a frame with `rect` (valid from
the previous frame's layout) and `state` (the retained `WidgetState`).

## Theming

Everything visual is a token in `ui::Theme` (see `include/ui/core/theme.hpp`).
Set a custom theme with `ctx.SetTheme(theme)` before the first frame.

| Token | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `panelBg` | `0x15191F` | Panel surface |
| `panelBorder` | `0x2A3038` | Panel hairline |
| `text` / `textDim` | `0xE6EDF3` / `0x8B949E` | Primary / secondary text |
| `accent` | `0x7FA8CC` | Interactive fill (buttons, active toggle, slider fill) |
| `accentHover` / `accentActive` | `0x94BBD9` / `0x6A92B7` | Hover / pressed accent |
| `controlBg`, `controlBorder`, `trackBg` | dark greys | Inactive control surfaces |
| `panelRadius` / `controlRadius` | 12 / 8 px | Corner radii |
| `shadowOffset` / `shadowBlur` / `shadowOpacity` | (0,6) / 16 / 0.28 | Panel shadow |
| `fontSize` / `rowGap` / `columnGap` / `controlHeight` | 15 / 10 / 12 / 34 px | Spacing metrics |

Previews of every state live in the repo: run `make preview` and read
`previews/buttons.png`, `previews/buttons-hover.png`, `previews/buttons-press.png`,
`previews/toggles.png`, `previews/sliders.png`.

---

# Layout

# Layout

Layout is powered by a vendored Yoga (flexbox) tree, exposed through an RAII
wrapper: `ui::LayoutNode`. You usually interact with it through panels and
groups rather than nodes directly.

## Panels

A panel is an absolutely positioned root node with a title, padding, border
and shadow. Panels are the *containers* of the retained layout tree — they are
identified by string id and reused across frames.

```cpp
ui::PanelStyle ps = ui::PanelStyle::FromTheme(ui::Theme::Default(), 18.f, "Title");
ctx.BeginPanel("main", ui::Rect(28, 28, 470, 640), ps);
// ... declare rows, columns, widgets ...
ctx.EndPanel();
```

- `Rect` is the on-screen position/size in pixels (y-down).
- `PanelStyle::FromTheme(theme, padding, title)` derives the standard look;
  every field is overridable (colors, radii, shadow, title size).
- `title` is optional; a `nullptr` title renders a borderless content panel.

## Rows and columns

```cpp
ctx.BeginRow();          // horizontal flex container
ctx.BeginColumn();       // vertical flex container inside a row
// ... widgets stack inside ...
ctx.EndGroup();          // closes the innermost open group
ctx.EndGroup();
```

`BeginRow()`/`BeginColumn()` are thin wrappers over `BeginGroup(bool row)`.
Groups use `rowGap`/`columnGap` from the theme and stretch children by
default. The demo runner builds a two-column panel exactly this way — see
`examples/common/AppSupport.hpp::BuildDemoUi`.

## Styling nodes directly

For custom layout behavior, use `ui::LayoutNode` (this is what the internals
use):

```cpp
ui::LayoutNode node;
node.SetFlexDirection(YGFlexDirectionRow);
node.SetGap(YGGutterColumn, 12.f);
node.SetFlexGrow(1.f);
node.SetPaddingAll(16.f);
node.SetWidth(400.f);
```

Computed rects read back with `LayoutLeft/Top/Width/Height()` (parent-relative)
or `ChildRect(parent)` for the absolute rect. The full Yoga style surface is
wrapped: flex, grow/shrink, align, gaps, padding/margin/border per edge,
min/max constraints, position type.

## One-frame latency

Widget rects come from the *previous* frame's layout. This is deliberate:

- input hit-testing never depends on work done later in the same frame;
- widgets can draw immediately with stable geometry;
- the cost is a single frame of delay when a panel resizes or first appears.

If you need a new panel to appear already laid out, declare it one frame
before making it visible (or accept the one-frame pop — it's imperceptible at
overlay frame rates).

---

# Rendering

# Rendering

The renderer draws everything as signed-distance fields in a single GL 3.3
core pipeline. No textures for shapes, no geometry for corners — a quad per
widget and a fragment shader that does the work.

## Pipeline per frame

1. Widgets record POD commands into `ui::CommandQueue`
   (`RoundedRect`, `Glyph`, `ClipPush`/`ClipPop`).
2. `Batcher` expands each command into padded quads (96-byte interleaved
   vertices) and batches: one draw for all rects, one draw per atlas/font-size
   run for glyphs.
3. `GlStateGuard` (RAII) saved the host's state before the pass and restores
   it afterwards — program, VAO/VBO/IBO bindings, blend func + equation,
   cull/depth/scissor, viewport, texture bindings, active texture, pixel
   store.

## Blend contract

The batcher **owns** blending for the UI pass and enables premultiplied
alpha:

```glsl
glEnable(GL_BLEND);
glBlendFuncSeparate(GL_ONE, GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA,
                    GL_ONE, GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA);
```

Every fragment the shaders emit is premultiplied (shadow is pure black with
alpha; fill/border/text are `rgb * a`). Host code that wants its state back
gets exactly what it had.

## Shape shader

Rounded rects are analytic SDFs with per-corner radii:

- antialiased fill via `fwidth`-scaled `smoothstep`
- inner border of configurable width and color
- soft drop shadow: the shadow SDF is the same rect offset by
  `shadowOffset`, grown by `shadowSpread`, with a `±shadowBlur` falloff,
  multiplied by `shadowOpacity`

## Text shader

Glyphs are MSDF (multi-channel signed distance fields) sampled from a single
atlas texture:

```glsl
float sd = median3(sample.rgb) - 0.5;
float screenPxRange = /* atlas pxRange scaled to the current font size */;
float alpha = clamp(sd * screenPxRange + 0.5, 0.0, 1.0);
```

`screenPxRange` is derived per-fragment from `fwidth(uv)` so text stays crisp
at any scale without regenerating anything.

## Clipping

`ClipPush`/`ClipPop` commands map to `glScissor` in y-down pixel coordinates.
The queue tracks depth (max 32) and pairs pushes/pops; nested panels and
text clipping compose naturally.

## Notes for custom backends

The command queue is pure data (see `include/ui/renderer/command_queue.hpp`).
`Context::SetDrawBackend()` sends `Render()` at a `DrawBackend`. With no
backend set, the OpenGL batcher runs inside `GlStateGuard`.

`FontAtlas::Load` keeps the atlas on the CPU (`Pixels()`, `Revision()`).
Each backend uploads. `TextureId()` is a stable batch key, not a GL name.

`DrawCircle` is a rounded rect. `DrawTriangle` is its own command (filled,
or stroked when `stroke` > 0). Lines and triangles share the quad SDF path
(`params.w` 2 and 3).

`VulkanRenderer` records into a command buffer the host already put inside
its render pass. Call `Prepare(atlas)` before the pass so font uploads are
not issued mid-pass. Backdrop blur is skipped on Vulkan.

Fill in `VulkanCreateInfo` fully: `renderPass`, `subpass`, `sampleCount` must
describe the pass the UI records in, and `framesInFlight` must match how many
frames the host keeps in flight (the renderer rotates its vertex buffer and
descriptor set across that many slots). Recreating the render pass — a
swapchain resize — invalidates the pipeline: call `Init()` again. `Prepare`
and `ReleaseDevice` wait for the device because they replace images.

`Context::DiscardFrame()` drops the recorded commands without drawing (the
host decided not to present this frame); `Context::ReleaseGraphics()` drops the
GPU objects of the active backend, for when the GL context or Vulkan device
goes away. The CPU-side atlas survives both, so the next frame re-uploads.

The shared vertex is `ui::UiVertex` (120 bytes). OpenGL tries `#version 330 core`,
then `330`, then `150`, so a compatibility context can still compile the shader.

---

# Fonts

# Fonts

Text is rendered using Multi-channel Signed Distance Field (MSDF) vector atlases. `aris-ui` supports two loading workflows:
1. **Direct TTF / OTF loading with automatic caching (`FontAtlas::LoadTtf`)**: Drop in any TrueType/OpenType font (including Google Fonts like Inter, Roboto, or JetBrains Mono) with one function call.
2. **Zero-dependency runtime loading (`FontAtlas::Load`)**: Load pre-baked PNG + JSON atlases with no FreeType dependency in shipped game injection overlays.

## Loading Custom Fonts (.ttf / .otf / Google Fonts)

You can load any TrueType or OpenType font directly. If the cached atlas files already exist and are up to date, `aris-ui` loads them instantly from disk; otherwise, it generates and caches the MSDF atlas automatically:

```cpp
ui::FontAtlas font;

// 1. One-line loading: automatically generates & caches under atlas/Inter
font.LoadTtf("assets/fonts/Inter.ttf");

// 2. Specify a custom cache prefix or generation parameters:
font.LoadTtf("fonts/Roboto-Bold.ttf", "atlas/roboto_bold", /*fontSize=*/48.f, /*pxRange=*/4.f);

ctx.SetFont(&font);
```

### Fetching Google Fonts

A CLI helper script `./tools/fetch_font.sh` is included to download any Google Font directly into `assets/fonts/`:

```sh
# Download standard Google Fonts by name:
./tools/fetch_font.sh Inter
./tools/fetch_font.sh Roboto
./tools/fetch_font.sh "JetBrains Mono"

# Or download from any custom URL:
./tools/fetch_font.sh https://example.com/MyFont.ttf
```

`aris-ui` comes bundled out-of-the-box with clean static TrueType builds of **Inter** (`assets/fonts/Inter.ttf`, `Inter-Regular.ttf`, `Inter-Bold.ttf`).

## Generating an atlas offline

For stripped-down game injection clients without FreeType:

From the CLI (built as `build/atlasgen`):

```sh
./build/atlasgen assets/fonts/Inter.ttf atlas/ui
```

Or from code:

```cpp
ui_atlas::Params params;
params.fontSize = 48.f;         // reference px size (em-normalization basis)
params.pxRange  = 4.f;          // MSDF distance range in atlas pixels
params.firstCodepoint = 32;     // default: printable ASCII
params.lastCodepoint  = 126;
params.extraChars = "\xC3\x97\xE2\x80\x94\xE2\x9C\x93";   // UTF-8 extras (×, —, ✓)

std::string err;
ui_atlas::GenerateAndWrite("assets/fonts/Inter.ttf", "atlas/ui", params, err);
```

`GenerateAndWrite` caches: outputs are regenerated only when the PNG is older
than the font file. Delete the pair after changing generator code.

## Runtime loading (Zero FreeType Dependency)

```cpp
ui::FontAtlas font;
if (!font.Load("atlas/ui.png", "atlas/ui.json")) { /* handle error */ }
ctx.SetFont(&font);
```

`Load` uploads the texture (needs a live GL context) and parses the metadata.
Metrics are em-normalized: glyph quads scale by `fontSize` at draw time, so
one atlas serves every size and DPI crisply.

> The atlas owns a GL texture. Call `font.Unload()` (or let it go out of
> scope) **before** your GL context is destroyed.

## JSON schema

```json
{
  "atlas":   { "width": 512, "height": 512 },
  "pxRange": 4,
  "metrics": { "fontSize": 48, "lineHeight": 1.17, "ascender": 0.93, "descender": -0.24 },
  "glyphs": [
    {
      "codepoint": 65,
      "advance": 0.684,
      "planeBounds": [0.008, 0.0, 0.676, 0.729],   // em units, y-up: l, b, r, t
      "atlasBounds": [179, 217, 32.06, 34.99]      // PNG pixels: x, y (top-left origin), w, h
    }
  ]
}
```

- `planeBounds` — glyph ink box in em units (multiplied by `fontSize` to get
  screen-space quads).
- `atlasBounds` — the ink rectangle in atlas pixels. The runtime maps
  `planeBounds` 1:1 onto this rect, so padding never distorts glyphs.
- `metrics` — em-normalized plane metrics; `Ascender(fontSize)` and
  `LineHeight(fontSize)` multiply them out.

## MSDF details (msdfgen v1.12 semantics)

The generator calls msdfgen with these invariants — keep them if you touch it:

- `loadGlyph(..., FONT_SCALING_EM_NORMALIZED)` → shape space is em.
- Projection is `pixel = scale * (shape + translate)` with translate in
  **shape units**: `translate = margin/fs - bounds.{l,b}`.
- `Range` is in the same units as the shape: `Range(pxRange / fs)`.
- `generateMSDF` applies error correction internally; no second pass needed.
- Glyphs are shelf-packed with `pxRange + 1` px separation, blitted after all
  placements so the row stride matches the final atlas size.

## Text layout

`ctx.DrawText` decodes UTF-8, resolves each codepoint through
`FontAtlas::GetGlyph` (falling back to `?`), advances the pen by
`advance * fontSize`, and positions quads at
`baseline - top * fontSize`. `ctx.MeasureText` sums the same advances —
useful for right-aligned labels (see the slider value text).

Shaping and kerning are not implemented yet (roadmap Stage 13).

---

# Agent Tooling

# Agent Tooling

aris-ui is built to be *changed by AI coding agents safely*. Everything in
this page exists so an agent can compile, verify, and **see** the result of
its edits without a human in the loop.

Read `AGENTS.md` in the repository root first — it is the agent contract
(repo map, commands, conventions, gotchas).

## One-command verification loop

```sh
make verify
```

Runs `make test` + `make preview`. After any change to rendering, widgets,
layout or fonts, this is the loop to run. It never needs a display.

## Visual previews (headless)

`aris_scene_preview` renders named UI scenes into an offscreen GLFW context
and writes PNGs — real framebuffer dumps, not mockups:

```sh
./build/aris_scene_preview --list                 # scene name<TAB>description
./build/aris_scene_preview --all --out previews   # render everything
./build/aris_scene_preview --scene panel,sliders --out previews
./build/aris_scene_preview --scene text --width 800 --height 600
```

| Scene | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| `panel` | The full canonical demo panel (all widgets) |
| `buttons` | Buttons, idle |
| `buttons-hover` | First button hovered (eased state, simulated mouse) |
| `buttons-press` | First button held down (simulated press) |
| `toggles` | Toggle on + off |
| `sliders` | Sliders at 0 / mid / full |
| `text` | MSDF text ramp 11–26 px + colored variants |
| `card` | SDF cards at radius 0 / 10 / 20 |

Behavior notes for agents writing scenes:

- `--warmup N` frames render before the snapshot so hover/press easing settles
  (default 10 ≈ 166 ms of simulated time).
- Simulated input is injected via `ctx.ProcessInput` before `BeginFrame`.
- Each scene gets a fresh `ui::Context`; the framebuffer is cleared per frame.
- Exit code is non-zero on unknown scene names or write failures — safe for
  CI.

## Tests

`make test` builds and runs `aris_tests` through CTest. The suite has zero
external dependencies (a ~100-line assert harness in `tests/test_main.hpp`)
and needs no GL context — it covers the pure logic:

- math: `Vec2/Vec4/Rect/Color` operators, blending, hex parsing
- easing: `ExpSmooth` frame-rate independence, monotonicity, `EaseOutCubic`,
  `EaseOutBack` overshoot, CSS `cubic-bezier` reference values
- ids: FNV-1a 64 against published reference vectors
- command queue: push/pop/clip-depth accounting, full `RectStyle` propagation
- widget state store: target convergence, no overshoot, GC staleness
- layout: Yoga two-column rows, gaps, stretch, padding, absolute `ChildRect`

Add a test file under `tests/`, add it to `aris_tests` in `CMakeLists.txt`,
follow the `TEST(name) { ... CHECK(...); }` pattern.

## Docs fetching (LLM-friendly)

- `docs/llms.txt` — index of documentation pages (the emerging llms.txt
  standard)
- `docs/llms-full.txt` — every documentation page concatenated in one file
- `docs-src/*.md` — the same content as plain Markdown, readable directly
  from the repository

The HTML site in `docs/` is generated by `tools/gen_docs.py` (stdlib-only)
from `docs-src/*.md`. Edit the Markdown, run `make docs`, commit both — the
sources are the single source of truth.

## GitHub Pages

The `docs/` folder is self-contained and designed to be served by GitHub
Pages: repository Settings → Pages → deploy from branch `main`, directory
`/docs`. No build workflow required.

## Instrumentation in the runner

The interactive runner takes environment switches — handy for agents even
though the preview tool is preferred:

- `ARIS_DUMP=N` — save the framebuffer as `dump_N.png` on frame N, then keep
  running
- `ARIS_DEBUG=1` — per-frame flush stats (vertex counts, atlas, px-range)

---
